# Gulf design integration checkpoint

**ID:** `evidence.checkpoints.regional-atlas`
**Status:** `evidence`
**Depends on:** `design.content.regional-promotion`, `mandate.evidence-obligations-m3-m4`
**Verifies:** `design.content.regional-promotion`, `design.content.catalog-authoring-boundary`, `design.representation.coalitions-sovereigns-and-geography`, `design.economy.external-provider-contracts`

**Inspected on the current working change:** the accepted Gulf rules now live in
their canonical owners. M4 world profiles require a source-backed complete
sovereign roster, typed coarse component bundles, component-owned cognition and
authority, explicit recorded or responsive political channels, and
deterministic rich-to-coarse reconciliation. Region scopes remain non-owning.
Resource processes, estimates, title, custody, transformations, delivery,
payments, accounts, observations, and feasible projects have distinct owners
and transitions.

The catalog inventory contains non-selectable candidate mappings for the two
historical Gulf lenses and the reusable Hormuz crisis template, including their
default Chair pairings and unresolved authoring obligations. It contains no new
world profile, selectable scenario, manifest, opening state, provider binding,
fixture, or calibration. The accepted M1 and M2 runtime boundaries remain
unchanged; the M4 mandate governs later implementation and evidence.
